story.head: Stephenson’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kraken have won two of the three meetings this season. The Flames come in at 6-7-0, the Kraken at 8-5-1. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames fifth (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Kraken third (tied for tenth). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Flames’ record (.462) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.444), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Flames do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). The Kraken keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. Seattle has allowed 3.71 goals a game, the third most in the league. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Joel Farabee (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matvei Gridin (5 G / 5 A / 10 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals, with seven points in his last five games. For the Kraken, Chandler Stephenson (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in seven straight games against Calgary. Frédérick Gaudreau (7 G / 3 A / 10 P in 14 GP) has a team-high seven goals.

Dustin Wolf (2-4-0 / .848 SV% in 6 GS) has struggled for Calgary so far, but will likely start. Seattle has two options in net: Philipp Grubauer (5-2-1 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) and Joey Daccord (3-3-0 / .880 SV% in 6 GS). Grubauer has started seven of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday, so Seattle could turn to Daccord to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Wolf has a .862 save percentage in seven starts against the Kraken, well under his usual .902. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Lane Lambert likes to send Winterton, Meyers and Douglas out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Tsyplakov, Castagna and Klapka.
